narrationTexts: I'll start by finding the remaining `db.query` call sites.
The vendor file is marked do-not-edit, so I'll leave that one and flag it. Reading the 11 remaining first-party files.
Now applying the migration — 3 call sites per file across 12 files.
Now verifying nothing is left and the files still parse.
finalText:
Migration finished. 36 call sites across 12 files moved from `db.query(sql, params)` to `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `repo/session.js`, `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `service/teamService.js` |
| billing | `repo/refund.js`, `service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `repo/supplier.js`, `admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `repo/shipment.js`, `service/returnService.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |
| support | `repo/sla.js`, `admin/macroAdmin.js` |

Each file had the same three sites (get-by-id, list, update); I matched the shape already used by the migrated siblings like `packages/accounts/src/repo/user.js`. All JS files pass `node --check`.

Two things I deliberately left alone:

- **`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js`** still has two `db.query` calls (lines 9 and 13). Its header says it's a vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4, replaced wholesale on upgrade with local edits silently lost — so patching it in-tree would be undone and wouldn't survive. It does need handling before the driver drops `query`: options are pinning/patching upstream, a `patch-package`-style patch, or wrapping the `db` handle passed into the adapter with a shim that forwards `query` to `execute`. Tell me which you'd prefer and I'll do it.
- **`cache.query(...)`** calls (in the `cachedX` helpers) are a different API — `lib/cache.js` takes a cache key, not SQL — so they're unrelated to this migration.
